Okay, squad, listen up. The swell is big this morning, about two meters, and the wind is offshore. Renato, you're in heat three, with surfers from Busselton, Albany and Geraldton. You have twenty minutes, and the judges count your two best waves. Now, if I were in your heat, I'd sit a little wide of the peak, because the biggest sets break there. If I had a choice between a small wave now and a big wave later, I'd wait for the big one. But don't wait all day. If you sat out there for ten minutes with no waves, you'd start to panic, and you don't want that. And remember, nobody is perfect in the first round. If you surfed this heat like you surf at home, you'd advance easily. Okay. Wax your boards. Your heat starts at nine thirty.

Mate, that was crazy. I got knocked out in heat two. I'm a bit upset, honestly. A great wave came in the first minute, and I hesitated. The guy from Albany took it, and he got an eight. If I could surf that heat again, I'd go on the first good wave. No thinking, just go. But you know what? It's one heat. If I were a pro, this would be a big problem. I'm fifteen. There's a Round 2 in May. So now I'm your number one fan. Your heat is next. If you got a good wave in the first five minutes, you'd feel calm for the rest of the heat. So go early. And if you advanced, I'd buy you a pie at the bakery. Deal? Go get them.
